ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: inventory-service: p99 latency above 1000ms for 5 minutes (since 12:43 UTC)
Alerting service: inventory
Alert time: 2026-08-23T12:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-08-23T11:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T14:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 5 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-08-23T13:00:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-08-23T12:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check the latency profile of inventory-service around the alert time.)
  Result: M-024: Change detected at 2026-08-23T12:30:00Z: mean 122.27 before, 3759.9 after (481.1 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-024] inventory.latency_p99_ms from 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=112.7 max=5785.54 mean=2080.99 last=5785.54; mean=2080.99. Change detected at 2026-08-23T12:30:00Z: mean 122.27 before, 3759.9 after (481.1 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z = 112.7 (lowest); 2026-08-23T12:30:00Z = 1063.86 (first point after the change); 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z = 5785.54 (last); 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z = 5785.54 (peak).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-08-23T13:00:00Z", "metric": "cpu_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-08-23T12:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if CPU usage spiked alongside latency.)
  Result: M-020: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-020] inventory.cpu_pct from 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=32.12 max=40.87 mean=36.71 last=35.65; mean=36.71. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z = 32.12 (lowest); 2026-08-23T12:50:00Z = 40.87 (peak); 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z = 35.65 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-08-23T12:50:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "limit": 30, "query": "error timeout slow database", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-08-23T12:30:00Z"} (asked because: Search for error or timeout logs in inventory-service around the time of the alert.)
  Result: 0 matching log lines.
Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-08-23T13:00:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-08-23T12:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if the database connection pool is exhausted or filling up.)
  Result: M-021: Change detected at 2026-08-23T12:35:00Z: mean 30.23 before, 54.65 after (12.6 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-021] inventory.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=26.79 max=66.98 mean=41.5 last=66.98; mean=41.5. Change detected at 2026-08-23T12:35:00Z: mean 30.23 before, 54.65 after (12.6 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-08-23T12:05:00Z = 26.79 (lowest); 2026-08-23T12:35:00Z = 40.39 (first point after the change); 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z = 66.98 (last); 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z = 66.98 (peak).
Step 5: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "slow database query missing index latency spike"} (asked because: Retrieve mitigation steps for slow queries and missing indexes.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-03-3 (similarity 0.72).
  [R-03-3] Slow query or missing index - How to confirm (similarity 0.72): Search the logs for slow query warnings and for query plans showing a full scan of a large table. Check whether a schema migration recently dropped or changed an index. The slowness is present at normal traffic, and a single query taking several seconds is the signature, rather than short queries waiting for a connection.
  [R-03-6] Slow query or missing index - Verify recovery (similarity 0.69): The slow query should disappear from the logs, its run time should return to milliseconds and request latency should recover. Check the connection pool afterwards to confirm it has drained back to normal.
  [R-03-1] Slow query or missing index - Summary (similarity 0.68): Requests to the database are slow. A query that used to be fast now takes seconds, usually because an index is missing or is no longer being used, and every request that depends on that query waits for it.

Previous hypotheses:
- slow_query_missing_index: Latency spiked dramatically without a CPU spike or error logs, but database connection pool usage increased significantly, suggesting queries are taking longer and holding connections. (evidence: M-024, M-020, M-021)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: Database connection pool usage increased significantly right around the time latency spiked, indicating potential connection contention or exhaustion. (evidence: M-024, M-021)
- downstream_timeout: Latency spiked drastically while CPU usage remained normal and no local errors were logged, which could also be explained by waiting on a slow downstream service or database dependency. (evidence: M-024, M-020)
